observations: M4Gpu holds an optional ARef<drm::Device<Driver>>; DRM registration is foreign-owned devres.
Platform unregister calls platform_driver_unregister; post_unbind drops private data after remove/devres.
DRM Registration Drop invokes drm_dev_unregister; no M4 Execution WorkItem join is present in that Rust entry point. C DRM unregister internals remain to trace.
Generic Arc WorkItem trampoline reconstructs the Arc and calls T::run; it contains no explicit module pin in this reviewed implementation.

DRM Device release intentionally leaves drop_in_place disabled, with an upstream HACK comment about uninitialized data. The stored data includes scheduler/RTKit state. Therefore eventual ARef release must not be treated as proof that data destructors execute.
M4 Execution completion fences precede the end of the worker callback. Existing generic scheduler module fixture does not qualify that pump or release path.
next: Trace C DRM unregister/file release and RTKit notification lifetime; compare initialized-device ownership with upstream cleanup APIs before choosing a minimal safe worker-join/resource-release fix. Do not enable generic drop_in_place blindly.
